status: PRE-REGISTERED — what applying the harness to the frontier does; from the measured mechanism
question: if the harness helps, why not put it on the biggest model?

findings.F1_capability_gain_shrinks_with_base_qua: harness capability gain: small +29.4pp -> frontier_open +8.2pp (diminishing: less headroom to the ceiling)
findings.F2_reliability_per_dollar_optimum_is_int: lowest cost-per-correct HARNESSED = small_open_1.5B (0.168); frontier_closed = 2.5, frontier_open = 7.678 -> the frontier is the WORST reliability-per-dollar despite the best absolute reliability
findings.F3_honesty_is_open_vs_closed_not_size: lowest confident-wrong = small_open_1.5B (0.05); the CLOSED frontier is FLOORED at 0.17 (black-box honesty only, launderable per audit-starvation) — an OPEN 1.5B beats a CLOSED 70B on honesty (0.05 vs 0.17)
findings.best_absolute_reliability: frontier_open_405B at 0.912 (yes, frontier+harness wins ABSOLUTE capability)

the_synthesis.not_a_competitor_the_ceiling: applying the harness to the frontier IS the ESCALATION TIER of the verified cascade (ADR-0030) — the design already contains it at the top
the_synthesis.the_design_is_the_router: the cascade routes to the cheapest tier that clears the task; frontier+harness fires ONLY when the small tier provably stalls (cheap-tier sufficiency, measured 8.3x cheaper at 0% escalation on strong-cheap-tier workloads, #2798)
the_synthesis.when_frontier+harness_is_right: when the task is ABOVE the small model's error threshold (raw capability needed, e.g. SWE-bench where small base~0), OR when absolute reliability outweighs cost (safety-critical). Then escalate — the cascade already does.
the_synthesis.the_owned_wedge: an OPEN model + white-box honesty harness beats a CLOSED frontier on axis B AT ANY SIZE, because the probe needs activations the closed model will not expose. This is the one axis size cannot buy back.

falsifiable_kills.F1: if harness capability gain does NOT shrink as base quality rises (frontier gains as much pp as small), the headroom/reachability model is wrong
falsifiable_kills.F2: if frontier+harness is NOT the worst cost-per-correct, the size-cost vs overhead-savings tradeoff does not favor small — the whole reliability-per-dollar thesis weakens
falsifiable_kills.F3: if a closed frontier's black-box honesty MATCHES the open probe floor, the white-box wedge is illusory and axis B is not owned

measured_anchors: audit-starvation: black-box confidence gates launderable (this session)
honesty probe needs activations = open weights (v1.10)
verified cascade 8.3x cheaper via cheap-tier sufficiency (#2798)
modeled_not_measured: all base/reach/cost numbers per config are ASSUMED-shape, re-verify
the overhead multipliers (repair-fires-less-at-low-q) are derived-direction, magnitude assumed
black-box vs white-box honesty floors are plausibility bounds, not measured head-to-head
honesty.what_this_concedes: frontier+harness DOES win absolute capability AND absolute reliability. the small-model bet is a RELIABILITY-PER-DOLLAR bet + an OPEN-WEIGHTS-HONESTY bet, NOT a capability bet. stated plainly.
